wave: W6 — the shared plan infrastructure, and the Web UI as its first consumer
directive: user, 2026-09-30: start from the Web; BOTH sides share the infrastructure and differ only in the UI layer

what_is_shared_now.approvalPhraseFor(planId): ONE implementation of the approval gate's phrase. It names the planId because that is the PRE-approval identity: at the moment the gate asks, no teamId exists to demand. The phrase is SERVED inside the payload rather than re-derived by each consumer, because two spellings of 'the thing you must type' make neither of them the contract.
what_is_shared_now.planForSession(workspace, sessionId): ONE plan projection. The /plan ROUTE calls it (Web) and mpdTeams.planFor calls it (TUI), so a surface cannot disagree with the Web panel about what is staged or what the gate demands.
what_is_shared_now.mpdTeams.planFor: the service face the TUI will read. It never throws: a broken staging file must redden a surface's empty state, not take its render down.

what_is_the_ui_layer.web: packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/src/team-view.ts polls /state AND /plan in ONE pass and draws a staged-plan section: wants N members, wants N tasks, and the exact phrase. Every string comes from the payload.
what_is_the_ui_layer.tui: NOT DONE — see the blocker below. Its UI is the same projection over mpdTeams.planFor.

why_one_pass_the_two_routes: they are two halves of one answer — the team as it exists after an approval and the plan that awaits one — and a panel that polled them separately could show a staged plan beside a team that approval had already replaced
why_a_staged_plan_shows_with_NO_team: the team record is materialised AT approval, so before one there is no record. The panel used to return its empty sentence in exactly the state a captain most needs to act on; it now renders the plan section instead. THIS IS THE SAME FACT that made the TUI panel render 'MPD approval — (none)'.
the_tui_blocker_restated: a staged plan is SESSION-scoped (.mpd/team/staging/<sessionId>.json) while the TUI surfaces are WORKSPACE-scoped; grep sessionId packages/mpd-tui-plugin/src/scenes.ts returns nothing. The shared projection is now reachable from the TUI, but the TUI still has no sessionId to call it with. The scene props DO carry a live `channel`, which is the likely source — that is the next investigation, not a guess to build on.
